title: Rural consumption per person
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  SECTION 2 — ECONOMY: WHAT A MONTH COSTS
subtitle:
Average monthly spending per person in rural India, HCES 2023-24.
Chhattisgarh ₹2,739. Sikkim ₹9,377. The national figure is ₹4,122.
callout_note: ₹ a month per person in rural {state}, the highest of any state or territory
takeaway: Rural spending per person runs from ₹2,739 in Chhattisgarh to ₹9,377 in Sikkim, a gap of 3.4 times inside one country.
policy: A single national poverty line converted at one price level treats these as the same economy. State-specific price deflators are not a refinement here, they are the difference between a real estimate and an arithmetic one.
takeaway_hi: ग्रामीण भारत में प्रति व्यक्ति मासिक खर्च छत्तीसगढ़ में ₹2,739 से लेकर सिक्किम में ₹9,377 तक है — एक ही देश के भीतर साढ़े तीन गुना का अंतर।

title: Urban consumption per person
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  SECTION 2 — ECONOMY: WHAT A MONTH COSTS
subtitle:
The same survey, urban areas. Chhattisgarh ₹4,927, Sikkim ₹13,927.
The urban figure exceeds the rural one in every state without exception.
callout_note: ₹ a month per person in urban {state}, against ₹6,996 nationally
takeaway: Urban spending per person is higher than rural spending in all 36 states and territories. The national gap is ₹6,996 against ₹4,122, about 70 per cent.
policy: Urban-rural is the axis most Indian transfer programmes are least able to see: entitlements are settled at the village or ward, while the gap that drives migration sits between them.
takeaway_hi: सभी 36 राज्यों और केंद्रशासित प्रदेशों में शहरी प्रति व्यक्ति खर्च ग्रामीण खर्च से अधिक है। राष्ट्रीय अंतर लगभग 70 प्रतिशत है।

title: Rural consumption inequality
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  SECTION 2 — ECONOMY: WHO GETS WHAT
callout_note: Gini in rural {state}, the widest rural spread in the country
takeaway: Kerala has the seventh highest rural spending per person of 36 states and territories and the second most unequal rural distribution, at a Gini of 0.255 against 0.237 nationally. A high average is not a flat one.
policy: Ranking states by mean consumption and ranking them by its dispersion produce different lists. Any transfer designed off the mean alone is targeting a state that does not exist.
takeaway_hi: केरल में ग्रामीण खर्च का स्तर भी ऊंचा है और उसका फैलाव भी — गिनी 0.255, राष्ट्रीय 0.237 के मुकाबले।

title: Urban consumption inequality
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  SECTION 2 — ECONOMY: WHO GETS WHAT
subtitle:
The same measure in urban areas: 0.284 nationally against 0.237 rural,
and higher than the rural figure in 31 of 36 states and territories.
Jharkhand and Ladakh are the widest, Nagaland and Manipur the narrowest.
callout_note: Gini in urban {state}, the widest urban spread in the country
takeaway: Urban consumption is more unequal than rural consumption in 31 of 36 states and territories. The five exceptions are small island and hill units. Jharkhand has among the lowest urban spending per person and the widest spread.
policy: Cities are where the dispersion is, and where the instruments are weakest: urban India has no counterpart to the rural employment guarantee.
takeaway_hi: लगभग हर राज्य में शहरी उपभोग ग्रामीण उपभोग से अधिक असमान है। झारखंड में शहरी खर्च कम है और फैलाव सबसे अधिक।

title: Female labour force participation
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  SECTION 4 — GENDER: WHO IS COUNTED AS WORKING
subtitle:
Women aged 15 and above working or looking for work, PLFS 2025.
Delhi 13.1 per cent. Sikkim 66.7. The national figure is 40.0.
callout_note: of women aged 15 and above are in the labour force in {state}
takeaway: Delhi records the lowest female labour force participation in the country at 13.1 per cent, five times below Sikkim's 66.7. Income and participation do not move together across states.
policy: Participation measured on usual status counts unpaid family labour on a farm and does not count housework. Much of the state-to-state range is a measurement boundary, and reading it as a preference is how the number gets misused.
takeaway_hi: दिल्ली में महिला श्रम बल भागीदारी देश में सबसे कम है, 13.1 प्रतिशत — सिक्किम के 66.7 से पाँच गुना कम।

title: Gender gap in literacy
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  SECTION 4 — GENDER: WHAT WAS NOT TAUGHT
callout_note: percentage points between male and female literacy in {state}
takeaway: Rajasthan's literacy gap is 23.2 percentage points, ten times Kerala's 2.2. The 14 states left grey are not included in the published round.
policy: A literacy gap among people aged 7 and above is an accumulated record, not a current one: it holds decades of school enrolment inside a single number, and closing it has a floor set by how long people live.
takeaway_hi: राजस्थान में साक्षरता का लैंगिक अंतर 23.2 प्रतिशत बिंदु है, केरल के 2.2 से दस गुना अधिक।

title: Child stunting, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: HOW TALL CHILDREN GROW
subtitle:
Children under 5 who are stunted, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Puducherry 16.6 per cent. Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu 37.1. India 29.3, down from 35.5 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of children under 5 are stunted in {state}, the highest of any state or territory with a figure
takeaway: Between 16.6 per cent in Puducherry and 37.1 per cent in Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, stunting still differs by more than two times across the country. The India figure fell from 35.5 to 29.3 per cent between NFHS-5 and NFHS-6.
policy: A national fall hides states that moved the other way. Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep rose, so a programme judged on the India average would miss them.
takeaway_hi: पुडुचेरी में 16.6 प्रतिशत से दादरा और नागर हवेली और दमन और दीव में 37.1 प्रतिशत तक, बौनापन अब भी दो गुना से अधिक अलग है। NFHS-5 से NFHS-6 के बीच भारत का आँकड़ा 35.5 से घटकर 29.3 प्रतिशत हो गया।

title: Institutional births, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: WHERE BIRTHS HAPPEN
subtitle:
Births in a health facility in the five years before the survey, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Nagaland 62.2 per cent. Lakshadweep 100.0. India 90.6, up from 88.6 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of births took place in a health facility in {state}
takeaway: Nearly every birth now happens in a facility in most states, with Lakshadweep at 100.0 per cent. Nagaland, at 62.2 per cent, is the clear outlier, and India stands at 90.6 per cent, up from 88.6.
policy: When the national figure is near 90 per cent, the remaining gap is concentrated in a few states and in the most remote households, and it needs targeted delivery rather than another national drive.
takeaway_hi: अधिकांश राज्यों में लगभग हर प्रसव अब स्वास्थ्य संस्थान में होता है, लक्षद्वीप में 100.0 प्रतिशत। नागालैंड 62.2 प्रतिशत के साथ स्पष्ट अपवाद है, और भारत का आँकड़ा 88.6 से बढ़कर 90.6 प्रतिशत है।

title: Women who have used the internet, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  EDUCATION: WHO IS ONLINE
subtitle:
Women aged 15-49 who have ever used the internet, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Tripura 48.8 per cent. Goa 94.0. India 64.3, nearly double the 33.3 of NFHS-5.
callout_note: of women aged 15-49 have ever used the internet in {state}
takeaway: The share of women who have ever used the internet nearly doubled between the two rounds, from 33.3 to 64.3 per cent. It still runs from 48.8 per cent in Tripura to 94.0 per cent in Goa.
policy: Ever having used the internet is a low bar. It says nothing about owning a phone, reading confidently online, or using a service independently, so it should not be read as digital inclusion.
takeaway_hi: दो दौर के बीच कभी इंटरनेट इस्तेमाल करने वाली महिलाओं का हिस्सा लगभग दोगुना होकर 33.3 से 64.3 प्रतिशत हो गया। फिर भी यह त्रिपुरा में 48.8 प्रतिशत से गोवा में 94.0 प्रतिशत तक है।
title_hi: इंटरनेट इस्तेमाल करने वाली महिलाएँ, NFHS-6

title: Women with a bank account they use, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  GENDER: WHO HOLDS THE ACCOUNT
subtitle:
Women aged 15-49 with a bank or savings account they themselves use, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Meghalaya 81.5 per cent. Ladakh 95.5. India 89.0, up from 78.6 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of women aged 15-49 have a bank or savings account they use themselves in {state}
takeaway: Access to an account women use themselves has become close to universal. The gap between states shrank to 14 points, from 81.5 per cent in Meghalaya to 95.5 per cent in Ladakh.
policy: An account that a woman uses herself is not the same as control over the money in it. Survey figures on decisions and earnings are the next question to ask.
takeaway_hi: महिलाओं द्वारा स्वयं उपयोग किए जाने वाले खाते की पहुँच लगभग सार्वभौमिक हो गई है। राज्यों के बीच अंतर घटकर 14 अंक रह गया, मेघालय में 81.5 प्रतिशत से लद्दाख में 95.5 प्रतिशत तक।
title_hi: स्वयं उपयोग किए जाने वाले बैंक खाते वाली महिलाएँ, NFHS-6

title: Spousal violence, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  GENDER: WHAT WOMEN REPORT
subtitle:
Ever-married women aged 18-49 who have ever experienced spousal violence, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Ladakh 1.9 per cent. Bihar 36.1. India 22.3, down from 29.2 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of ever-married women aged 18-49 report spousal violence in {state}
takeaway: Reported spousal violence runs from 1.9 per cent in Ladakh to 36.1 per cent in Bihar. The India figure is 22.3 per cent, down from 29.2 in NFHS-5.
policy: These are what women told interviewers, and a low figure can mean low violence or low willingness to report it. Some state changes between rounds are very large, so read a single state with care.
takeaway_hi: रिपोर्ट की गई पति द्वारा हिंसा लद्दाख में 1.9 प्रतिशत से बिहार में 36.1 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 22.3 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 29.2 था।

title: Women married before 18, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  GENDER: HOW EARLY MARRIAGE HAPPENS
subtitle:
Women aged 20-24 who were married before age 18, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Kerala 2.9 per cent. West Bengal 36.4. India 20.1, down from 23.3 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of women aged 20-24 were married before 18 in {state}
takeaway: Child marriage fell nationally from 23.3 to 20.1 per cent, but it is still 36.4 per cent in West Bengal, more than twelve times the 2.9 per cent of Kerala.
policy: Andaman and Nicobar and Tamil Nadu have no published figure in the fact sheets, so they are grey. A grey state here has no figure, not a low one.
takeaway_hi: बाल विवाह राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर 23.3 से घटकर 20.1 प्रतिशत हुआ, पर पश्चिम बंगाल में यह अब भी 36.4 प्रतिशत है, जो केरल के 2.9 प्रतिशत से बारह गुना से अधिक है।
